exposure: Mode of delivery (emergency cesarean section vs. vacuum-assisted delivery)
outcome: Composite adverse neonatal outcome (Apgar score < 7 at 5 minutes, respiratory distress syndrome, neonatal intensive care unit admission, mechanical ventilation, intrapartum fetal death)
cohort: 611 women who underwent either emergency cesarean delivery or vacuum-assisted delivery during the second stage of labor and delivered neonates with a birthweight of <2500 g between 2011 and 2019
finding: Neonatal and maternal outcomes did not differ substantially between emergency cesarean delivery and vacuum-assisted delivery for neonates weighing <2500 g.
mod_finding: While the rate of Apgar score < 7 at 1 minute was higher in the emergency cesarean delivery group, other neonatal and maternal outcomes were similar between emergency cesarean delivery and vacuum-assisted delivery.
